The facts of the case are that a FIR was lodged on 15.6.2014 by the opposite party no.2 against seven persons including the applicant with the allegations that he is a Molvi by profession and teaches students and treats the ailments by prayers.

In the last week of February, 2014, four persons came to him who disclosed their names as Parvej, Ashraf, Yaqoob and Shabbir (the present applicant) and told him that they want to get a lady treated who is ill.
They appreciated the work of Molvi and after some days stated that the condition of the lady is improving.
The relationship between the persons and the complainant started developing as they used to often visit him.
On 20.3.2014 at about 1 p.m. all the four persons came to him and told that they have a land in Bijnor which is very ably situated.
They have spent a lot of money in treatment of the mother of Parvej and have landed up in a loss due to it.
They need money, as such they want to sell the said property.
They showed a khatauni to the complainant in which the names of four persons were shown to be endorsed.
They also took him to the plot and showed it.
On 29.3.2014 at about 12 p.m., they came to him and settled the transaction in Rs.9,00,000/-.
Rs.3,50,000/- was given to them for which they issued a receipt and it was decided that the sale-deed would be executed in next ten days.
After three days Shabbir and Yaqoob came and demanded Rs.20,000/- and told that the said money be also added in the transaction.
After 10 days he told the persons to get the sale-deed executed, they did not get it done.
On being suspicious, he went to Bijnor and to get the documents verified and came to know that the khatauni was forged document.
He demanded Rs.3,70,000/- from them, then they refused and started abusing him, assaulted him and threatened.
On 15.6.2014, the accused persons came to him and demanded the remaining amount of money and said that they would execute the sale-deed.
The said persons were got apprehended by the first informant with the help of other persons and have been brought by them at the police station.
The FIR was thus lodged.
The matter was investigated and charge sheet was submitted against the accused persons after which Parvej had died and as such the case was expunged for him.
The trial court took cognizance upon the said charge sheet and summoned the said accused persons vide order dated 3.7.2015.
Subsequently since the accused did not appear, the trial court issued process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and NBW vide order dated 1.9.2015.
The same is continuing till date.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that no such documents were ever shown by the applicants to the complainant.
It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the applicant showed any documents to the complainant and on that false pretext took money from him.
It is argued that the implication of the applicant in the present case is with malafide intention and the present case is a totally false and concocted case.
The present proceedings against the applicant are abuse of process of Court and as such deserves to be quashed.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the state opposed the prayer for quashing.
7. After having heard learned counsel for both the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is named in the FIR.
There are allegations against him.
In so far as truthfulness of the allegations are concerned, this Court in an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot go into the same.
The same is subject matter of trial.
The applicant has been summoned vide order dated 3.7.2015.
The applicant as per FIR itself was apprehended and brought to the police station and was released on bail.

Subsequent of filing of charge sheet and summoning, the applicant did not appear Shabbir vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117484007/
2 before the trial court and NBW were issued against him and since the year 2015, it has been eight years.

sentences.text: After about eight years of taking cognizance and summoning and also of issuance of NBW, the applicant has approached this Court in a application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. Prima-facie allegations are there against the applicant.

It is trite law that malafide intentions of the complainant cannot be a ground for quashing as has been held by the Apex Court in the case of State of M.P. v.
Awadh Kishore Gupta : (2004) 1 SCC 691.
